title: Salt in the Wire
audience: adult literary / quiet speculative readers who like moral ambiguity and restraint
reader_contract: a concrete central question with no clean answer
the ending withholds comfort; ambiguity is intended, not evasive
no supernatural element; the strangeness is moral, not physical
theme_question: When following the rule would kill and breaking it saved lives, is inherited silence a betrayal or a mercy?
desired_affect: unease that outlasts the last line
constraints: no storm or outsider as the cause of the fault
no villain; the antagonist force is duty itself
Mara must act, not merely understand
prose earns emotion through behavior, never names it
